programme.title: Keynote: Michael Saylor | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The credit market just got a new heavyweight. In this keynote, Michael Saylor reveals how Strategy engineered STRC, a Bitcoin-backed preferred stock that grew into the largest and most liquid preferred in the world in under eight months. Saylor breaks down the math behind 11.5% tax-deferred yields, why private credit is melting down, and how digital credit is set to cannibalize trillions in legacy capital markets.

programme.desc: What does the ideal Bitcoin company actually look like? In this Bitcoin 2026 keynote, Jack Mallers CEO of Strike and Twenty One wears both hats to unveil a strategic merger with Tether's mining arm Electron and a slate of new Strike products including Volatility Proof Loans, lending proof of reserves, and a $2.1 billion credit facility. Jack walks through his four-quadrant framework that separates real Bitcoin companies from crypto casinos and treasury-only plays. If you care about Bitcoin-backed credit, mining, or capital markets strategy, this one is essential.

programme.desc: Afroman lit up the Bitcoin Conference stage in Las Vegas with a performance unlike anything else this year. After his house was raided and his money seized, he discovered that freedom of speech and Bitcoin were the tools he needed to fight back. In this set, he announces his 2028 presidential campaign, calls for jury trials in family court, and performs live renditions of "Because I Got High" and "Lemon Pound Cake." Don't miss this raw, hilarious, and unexpectedly powerful moment from Vegas.

programme.title: Tim Draper's Bitcoin Warning: A Run on the Banks Is Coming | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: The dollar is changing faster than most people realize. In this powerful keynote from The Bitcoin Conference in Las Vegas, legendary venture capitalist Tim Draper of Draper Associates explains why holding Bitcoin has shifted from opportunity to necessity. Drawing from his Mount Gox losses, his record-setting U.S. Marshal's Office auction bid, and decades of experience in Silicon Valley, Draper lays out the case for a dollar-to-stablecoin-to-Bitcoin transition.

programme.title: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins Bitcoin 2026 Fireside Chat
programme.desc: For the first time in history, a sitting SEC Chairman took the stage at the Bitcoin Conference. Paul Atkins joins Perianne Boring of The Digital Chamber on the Nakamoto stage in Las Vegas to detail a complete 180 in how the agency views digital assets. He breaks down the new joint token taxonomy with the CFTC, the SEC's reinterpretation of the Howey Test, and the upcoming innovation exemption that will let firms experiment with on-chain securities and token fundraising in the United States. If you want to understand where U.S. digital asset regulation is actually heading, this is the conversation.

programme.title: Fireside: CFTC Chairman Mike Selig | Bitcoin 2026
programme.desc: For more than a decade, Bitcoiners and developers have lived under regulatory uncertainty and sometimes outright hostility from Washington. In this fireside conversation, CFTC Chairman Mike Selig joins Gregory Xethalis to explain how the agency has used its first 100+ days to end regulation by enforcement, launch Project Crypto with the SEC, and protect software developers building on Bitcoin. Selig breaks down the new joint taxonomy guidance, the no-action letter for self-custodial wallets, and why pending market structure legislation is essential to future-proof the asset class.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Zapote, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Zapote is located 20 kilometers west of Puerto Morelos. Cenote Zapote is named after the Sapote trees growing nearby. It is located on the “Ruta de los Cenotes” the old road from Puerto Morelos to Valladolid. Zapote has quite a deep drop from the land surface to the water surface of 6m/20ft but its access is easy via stairs. The walls will rise above you like a fortress and once you start your descent they become narrower until a depth of 20m/66ft before starting to open back up again. Once you reach a depth of 30m/100ft you will be above the talus cone in a bell shaped chamber with a narrow skylight in the top through which you just descended. Halocline and a thin misty layer of Hydrogen Sulfide floating on top of it, as well as some of the most amazing and incredible formations commonly described as bells, elephant feet, shower heads or trumpets will truly take your breath away with their strange beauty and impressive size.

programme.title: Dive Site Saporkren at Night, Raja Ampat, Indonesia
programme.desc: The village of Saporken is located on the island of Waigeo, close to the capital town of Waisai. This site is typically dived at night, however day diving is good too. Saporkren is your typical sandy bottom muck dive site, which is a little grubby since its just off of the village jetty. Making your way down a gentle slope (with little or no current) past a few coral bommies, the best bit of Saporkren is generally around 12-20 metres. We found full-size seahorses, cute bobtail squid, flying flatworms, clownfish anemones, colemani shrimp plus many unusual crabs species such as the boxer, xeno and porcelain.

programme.title: Padar island, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Padar island is located in the middle of the straight between Rinca and Komodo Island. Padar is the third largest island in the Komodo National Park. It is located in the south central of the park, between Komodo and Rinca Island. In the past, Padar was one of the island in Komodo where there were dragons live. Along with the illegal hunting activities by human being, they are slowly disappeared and almost unable to see them anymore. The cause is simply because of the lack of foods, like deer and wild boar. Their extinction can be because they just died alone without any food to eat or prolonged hunger or they can be migrated to nearest island, Rinca. The island now remains empty with no dragons. However, other wild animals such as wild boars are still around daily. Today, Padar has become one of the most popular place to visit in Indonesia. It offers super magnificent view from the top of the island with pink sandy beach on the west side and white sandy beach on the east side. Formation of towering hill, just like Jurassic park. Although the island has no dragons existed, the island is one of the best charming spot of trekking. Those who love photographic, this is perhaps the best place for spectacular photos.

programme.title: Dive Site C56 Shipwreck, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: C-56 Shipwreck dive site is located in Puerto Morelos. The C-56 shipwreck served in World War II and it was sold to the Mexican Marine in 1966. The time pass by and later on 28th Oct 2000 was purposefully sunk, as a new attraction for divers coming to the Riviera Maya. Laying perfectly upright, with the keel on the sand at 90ft, the 184ft long Mexican Gun Boat was quickly inhabited by various marine life. The deck, at 64ft, is teeming with life and it's common to see a large shoal of Big Eye Travellies hunting there. As we travel around the wreck we commonly see large Wrasse, Groupers, Morays and, looking up, flights of Eagle Rays. Soft corals have colonized the wreck and now offer a home to many Arrow crabs and Fire worms amongst other small crustaceans and invertebrates.

programme.title: Sumidero Canyon, Tuxtla Gutiérrez , Mexico
programme.desc: Sumidero Canyon is located just north of the city of Tuxtla Gutiérrez. Sumidero Canyon (Spanish: Cañón del Sumidero) is a deep natural canyon which creation began around the same time as the Grand Canyon in the U.S. by a crack in the area's crust and subsequent erosion by the Grijalva River, which still runs through it. Sumidero Canyon has vertical walls which reach as high as 1,000 metres, with the river turning up to 90 degrees during the 13 kilometre length of the narrow passage.

programme.title: Wayag Island, Raja Ampat, Indonesia
programme.desc: Wayag Island is located on the far northwestern tip of Raja Ampat. The island is known for its beautiful atolls and amazing underwater life covering a total area of 155,000 hectares, about 383,013.3 acres. Here, you find pristine beaches with unique Karst islands that look like mushrooms sprouting out from the sea. Along these beaches, tourists can see fairy tale panorama, more captivating than Leonardo DiCaprio’s getaway in “The Beach”. The crystal clear waters around Wayag Island appear like unreal windows to various types of flora and fauna that live underwater.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Dos Ojos, Tulum, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Dos Ojos is located 15 kilometers north of Tulum. Dos Ojos (Two Eyes) refers to two neighboring cenotes that are connected by a large cavern that also connects to a subterranean river. The original explorations of this water system, one of the largest in the world, started in the Dos Ojos cenotes. The total length of the combined system was measured at 310.95 kilometers (193.22 mi). This cenote dive site consists of two independent circuits: The first dive starts at the Barbie Line, a 415 meters line with wide spaces and large light galleries. The second dive circuit is called the Bat Cave, a very different experience. The Bat Cave is an adjacent cenote, next to Dos Ojos, and represents a much more preserved environment, mainly due the fact that the roof of the cenote hasn’t collapsed yet and all of the formations around it are in very good shape.

programme.title: Dive Site Siaba Besar, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Siaba Besar dive site is located in the Central part of the Komodo National Park. Siaba Besar dive site is a sheltered bay with coral seamounts and amazing coral reefs, located in the North-West side of the island. The reef is 4-6 meters deep with healthy corals and sand patches around. It has a massive coral garden and lacks strong currents, but it does not mean it lacks cool sights and marine life, just the opposite! This feature makes Siaba Besar a suitable dive site for any kind of level, being the best place for those who have never dived and want to try this amazing experience in Komodo National Park. Siaba Besar is heaven for snorkelers, given its easy conditions with shallow coral reefs, very little current and abundant marine life. A superlative snorkeling among sea turtles it is guaranteed, which gives the nickname to this site: Turtle City

programme.title: Dive Site Manta Point, Nusa Penida, Indonesia
programme.desc: In this episode, you will explore Manta Point, located in Nusa Penida, Bali, Indonesia, and learn about its remarkable marine inhabitants. Manta Point, situated on Nusa Penida's southwest coast, is renowned for its resident Manta ray colony, making it a must-visit dive site. Divers of all levels are drawn to its diverse range of underwater experiences, including reef exploration, photography, training, and fish identification. Notable species found here include the day octopus and the tawny nurse shark, both captivating creatures. Manta rays, particularly the Manta alfredi species, gracefully glide through the water with their distinctive pectoral fins and are often seen at cleaning stations, where cleaner fish help them rid parasites. However, these majestic creatures face threats from overfishing and human impacts. Manta Point offers an extraordinary underwater adventure, showcasing the beauty and diversity of marine life in this region.

programme.title: The Komodo dragons of south Rinca, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Horseshoe Bay is located in the south of Rinca island, it is formed by Rinca island in the north and Nusa Kode in the south. The area is well known to be one of the best place to see wild Komodo dragons. The Komodo dragon (Varanus komodoensis), also known as the Komodo monitor, is a member of the monitor lizard family Varanidae that is endemic to the Indonesian islands of Komodo, Rinca, Flores, and Gili Motang. It is the largest extant species of lizard, growing to a maximum length of 3 metres, and weighing up to approximately 70 kilograms. As a result of their size, Komodo dragons are apex predators, and dominate the ecosystems in which they live. Komodo dragons hunt and ambush prey including invertebrates, birds, and mammals. It has been claimed that they have a venomous bite; there are two glands in the lower jaw that secrete several toxic proteins. The biological significance of these proteins is disputed, but the glands have been shown to secrete an anticoagulant. Komodo dragons' group behavior in hunting is exceptional in the reptile world. The diet of Komodo dragons mainly consists of Javan rusa (Rusa timorensis), though they also eat considerable amounts of carrion. Komodo dragons also occasionally attack humans.

programme.title: Lawa Darat island, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Lawa Darat island is located in the northern part of the Komodo National Park. Also known as the “island close to the land” has a barren, desert savannah that changes color from green to yellow depending on the season. The island features easy hiking trails and two viewpoints to suit both spectacular sunrise and sunsets. Lawa Darat island is well protected from strong winds and waves, making the island the perfect spot for various activities to be carried out in safety. Some even refer to the island as the Komodo’s fjord, as attributed to its geological position. Besides, Lawa Darat island’s proximity to the ocean crossroads enables visitors to experience unexpected marine surprises such as encountering the humpback or the blue whale emerging majestically from the sea. The main attraction of Lawa Darat island is the scenic view that awaits visitors as they trek and reach the peak. This sole reason is what drives most Komodo National Park visitors to land on this island. Although beautiful all day long, the best recommended time to trek to the peak is sunset, when the breathtaking panoramic view calls for an Instagram selfie. The vantage point makes it perfect for capturing the beautiful beaches or the rolling hills catching rays of light. Trekking to the peak of the island might be considered as quite challenging for some, in particular, the beginners, but it is incredibly doable and worthwhile. The view is better and more beautiful as you trek higher where the reef becomes clearer while the mountainside begins to glow. Be ready for the remarkable panorama that awaits you at the top where the Komodo National Park lies in the opposite.

programme.title: Dive Site Manta Alley, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Manta Alley dive site is located at the far southern end of Komodo Island in the Indian Ocean. Manta Alley consists of a series of small rocky islands a few hundred meters away from the main island. There are several spots around these rocks where mantas can be found almost all year round. The site starts in a shallow reef close to the shore, where you can expect a strong to mild drift dive. You should keep your eyes wide open just as you enter the water, as mantas can be often found right in the shallows. Manta Rays are coming to this area for mating and cleaning purposes, where small wrasse and butterfly fish clean the mantas of parasites. The cleaning station is around 20 meters, where the rocks meet a white sandy bottom, perfect spot to watch mantas gliding into the rocks. Though mantas are the main attraction of this site, Manta Alley it is also full of marine life including reef sharks, schools of trevallies and large wrasses. The corals are very beautiful and diverse as well, making this spot a spectacular background for marine life photography.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Maravilla, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Maravilla is located 10 kilometers west of Puerto Morelos. The cenote is a sinkhole in the shape of a bell, where the entrance is a hole in the middle of the top. The thick sulfur cloud offers views that look from another planet. Getting close to this cloud is necessary to observe the gorgeous living stalactites, the biothems often called “Hell’s bells.” Those mysterious rock formations are alive and grow underwater thanks to extraordinary endemic bacteria. This type of speleothems, called “elephant feet,” has been found in only 4 cenotes, all in the Puerto Morelos area and are subject to ongoing scientific research.

programme.title: Dive Site Siaba Kecil, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Siaba Kecil dive site is located in the Central part of the Komodo National Park. The best time to dive this site is when the current is running! This is a real rollercoaster of a ride and will often be referred to as the 'Superman drift'. This gorgeous coral reef with a stunning overhang has a fast moving current - nothing scary just a great drift along. No need to kick! Towards the end of the dive site you drift towards and more sheltered area and the current eases off. Here you can relax (catch your breath!), and admire the stunning hard corals and thousands on anthias. This is also a great spot for seeing hawksbill turtles. The strong currents of this dive site attract large fish including giant trevally, barracuda, tuna, sharks and the odd ray too! The overhangs provide a fascinating topography and if the current allows they are great to explore and hunt for nurse sharks, bamboo sharks and other bizarre creatures.

programme.title: Batu Bolong north, Komodo, Indonesia
programme.desc: You are about to go on a fascinating journey through the amazing underwater world of Batu Bolong. As you watch this remarkable documentary, you will discover the wonderful beauty and diversity of life below the waves. Located within Indonesia's Komodo National Park, Batu Bolong's exposed rock pinnacle reveals a hidden paradise full of marine wonders. Despite challenges like changing currents and depths, you will learn how expert divers navigate the currents and explore different depths, from shallow coral gardens to tall walls. You will see the vibrant underwater dance of reef fish, including colorful groupers, moray eels, and majestic emperor fish. You will encounter the mysterious white tip reef shark, marvel at its unique anatomy, and understand its interesting behaviors. As the documentary reveals the top predator, the giant trevally, you will be captivated by its striking features and hunting skills. You will delve into the complex relationships within the ecosystem, from cleaner fish caring for their companions to the vital role of table corals in sheltering marine life. Immerse yourself in this kaleidoscope of colors, shapes, and behaviors, and let the enchanting beauty of Batu Bolong's underwater world leave you longing for more, ready to return to this aquatic oasis time and again.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Angelita, Tulum, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Angelita is located 10 kilometers west of Tulum. Angelita is a magical cenote that is often described as mysterious and a bit spooky. At first, the cenote appears to be unassuming, just a small pond in the middle of a very thick jungle. However, the deepest parts of the cenote go down to 204 ft (66 m). Its most amazing feature is a 4.5 ft (1.5 m) thick hydrogen sulfide cloud that starts at 83 ft (27 m). This cloud is made up of gases that have leaked out of decomposing trees and leaves that fall from the jungle into the cenote. This gas accumulates where the fresh and the salt water meet (the halocline). This creates a false floor at the bottom, which can be traversed to reach a dark, otherworldly chamber that is full of jungle detritus. The base of this mountain of detritus starts below but reaches above the cloud. Rising again from below the cloud, the peak of the mountain of detritus takes on a new face, as if one is ascending a cloud-topped mountain. On the way out of the cenote, there is a small cave loop, and at the surface, one can get an appreciation for all of the trees that provide this cenote with its hydrogen sulfide cloud.

programme.title: Dive Site Paradise Reef, Cozumel, Mexico
programme.desc: Paradise Reef dive site is located in the west of Cozumel. Paradise Reef is the first reef when entering the Marine Park. The current runs from south to north normally. You will start across from the entrance to the Caleta and drift north. There are 2-3 coral ridges that parallel the shoreline. You can see schools of Grunts, Snappers, and Sergeant Majors, many Queen Angelfish. There are nice coral heads ranging from 3-6m tall that jut out from a sandy bottom. You can find anemones, and an assortment of nice sponges clinging to the coral heads. Just about every kind of fish from the area can be found here. Some of the bigger animals include barracuda and grouper. Keep a close eye for the small denizens such as Spotted Drum, Smooth Trunkfish, Spotted Moray Eels, and Spiny Lobster.

programme.title: Lawalaut Island, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Lawalaut Island is located northeast of Gili Lawa Darat Island. Gili Lawa Laut is understandably a magnet for visitors on land and sea. The island is in the Lesser Sunda Islands and sits to the north of Komodo Island and the other small islet of Gili Lawa Daret and as such is protected as part of the Komodo National Park. Geologically the islets are volcanic like much of the region and they have beautiful hills popular with hikers who come for the stunning views and secluded beaches. The island is uninhabited but has numerous trails for walking up the hills to see the surrounding area. The wildlife above water is slightly less of a draw than the sea life on this island as there is less vegetation than in other areas. The hills are grassy though, and the landscape is very beautiful and a popular photography spot for visitors to the national park.

programme.title: Arborek Island, Raja Ampat, Indonesia
programme.desc: Arborek is a tiny island in Raja Ampat archipelago, on west Papua. It is easily walkable on foot, taking roughly thirty minutes to walk the entire coastline. The island is known for its very hospitable tourism village and exceptional handicrafts with a thriving souvenir community. Be ready to be greeted with open arms by everyone, with many children who are eager to be photographed. This authentic island welcomes guests with pride, the islanders are happy to introduce all to the Papuan culture and unique traditional foods. It is a perfect paradise to learn a bit of the Asai culture, which is still kept alive in this isolated place. Arborek island, traditionally a mooring spot for boatmen, is surrounded by splendid sago palms, nourished by fish and it is sparsely populated by a tiny population of around 200 residents, spread in around 40 families. The water is crystal clear, with white fine sand and many coconut trees and bushes, providing a quite comforting and refreshing atmosphere. At the wooden pier you will find some gazebos, ideal for relaxing.

programme.title: Dive Site Yucab, Cozumel, Mexico
programme.desc: Yucab dive site is located in front of Mia beach in the west of Cozumel. There is a huge concentration of marine life which covers this reef. There are sponges everywhere and of every color. The sand scoured overhangs offer refuge for lobsters, banded coral shrimps and the arrow crab. There are also large numbers of squirrelfish, angel and butterflyfish always swimming in pairs. This is a great site for photographers.

programme.title: Dive Site Paso Del Cedral, Cozumel, Mexico
programme.desc: Paso Del Cedral dive site is located in front of El Cedral in the south west of Cozumel. Also called Cedral Wall it is one of the most beautiful dive sites in Cozumel. It can be done as a wall dive or closer to shore over the reef. The part of the reef that is not a wall, consists of a mile of sloping hills covered in sponges and coral. The reef bottoms out at about 18 meters (60 feet). As for the current, it's generally moderate to strong. As you drift you'll get to see eagle rays, lobsters, hawksbill turtles, green morays, big pufferfish, toadfish, and even sharks.

programme.title: Dive Site Cenote Zapote, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: Cenote Zapote is located 20 kilometers west of Puerto Morelos. Cenote Zapote is named after the Sapote trees growing nearby. It is located on the “Ruta de los Cenotes” the old road from Puerto Morelos to Valladolid. Zapote has quite a deep drop from the land surface to the water surface of 6m/20ft but its access is easy via stairs. The walls will rise above you like a fortress and once you start your descent they become narrower until a depth of 20m/66ft before starting to open back up again. Once you reach a depth of 30m/100ft you will be above the talus cone in a bell shaped chamber with a narrow skylight in the top through which you just descended. Halocline and a thin misty layer of Hydrogen Sulfide floating on top of it, as well as some of the most amazing and incredible formations commonly described as bells, elephant feet, shower heads or trumpets will truly take your breath away with their strange beauty and impressive size.

programme.title: Dive Site Saporkren at Night, Raja Ampat, Indonesia
programme.desc: The village of Saporken is located on the island of Waigeo, close to the capital town of Waisai. This site is typically dived at night, however day diving is good too. Saporkren is your typical sandy bottom muck dive site, which is a little grubby since its just off of the village jetty. Making your way down a gentle slope (with little or no current) past a few coral bommies, the best bit of Saporkren is generally around 12-20 metres. We found full-size seahorses, cute bobtail squid, flying flatworms, clownfish anemones, colemani shrimp plus many unusual crabs species such as the boxer, xeno and porcelain.

programme.title: Padar island, Komodo National Park, Indonesia
programme.desc: Padar island is located in the middle of the straight between Rinca and Komodo Island. Padar is the third largest island in the Komodo National Park. It is located in the south central of the park, between Komodo and Rinca Island. In the past, Padar was one of the island in Komodo where there were dragons live. Along with the illegal hunting activities by human being, they are slowly disappeared and almost unable to see them anymore. The cause is simply because of the lack of foods, like deer and wild boar. Their extinction can be because they just died alone without any food to eat or prolonged hunger or they can be migrated to nearest island, Rinca. The island now remains empty with no dragons. However, other wild animals such as wild boars are still around daily. Today, Padar has become one of the most popular place to visit in Indonesia. It offers super magnificent view from the top of the island with pink sandy beach on the west side and white sandy beach on the east side. Formation of towering hill, just like Jurassic park. Although the island has no dragons existed, the island is one of the best charming spot of trekking. Those who love photographic, this is perhaps the best place for spectacular photos.

programme.title: Dive Site C56 Shipwreck, Puerto Morelos, Mexico
programme.desc: C-56 Shipwreck dive site is located in Puerto Morelos. The C-56 shipwreck served in World War II and it was sold to the Mexican Marine in 1966. The time pass by and later on 28th Oct 2000 was purposefully sunk, as a new attraction for divers coming to the Riviera Maya. Laying perfectly upright, with the keel on the sand at 90ft, the 184ft long Mexican Gun Boat was quickly inhabited by various marine life. The deck, at 64ft, is teeming with life and it's common to see a large shoal of Big Eye Travellies hunting there. As we travel around the wreck we commonly see large Wrasse, Groupers, Morays and, looking up, flights of Eagle Rays. Soft corals have colonized the wreck and now offer a home to many Arrow crabs and Fire worms amongst other small crustaceans and invertebrates.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

Based on the international bestselling book of the same name, by Dr. Michael Greger, this movie plays like a fast-paced action thriller but is packed with hard-hitting data that just might save your life. How Not to Die exposes the role of the standard Western diet in fueling today’s most widespread illnesses. The film offers jaw-dropping, but evidence-based, insights into the prevention of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, kidney disease, liver dysfunction, and a spectrum of brain disorders, including dementia and Alzheimer’s disease. It also addresses how diet influences the development of colon, prostate, and other digestive cancers, delivering life-saving information with clarity and authority.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.title: Khan Palace
programme.desc: We show you one of the best heritage of cultural tourism, as known The Khan's Palace. In the Crimean heartland, the longest-lived of the Turkic khanates left an even more enduring landmark, The Khan's Palace; in other words, home to the Crimean Tatars. Raised in the 16th century, Khan’s Palace served as a palace for the representatives of the Giray dynasty. Located in the city of Bakhchisaray, the palace was the political, spiritual, and cultural epicenter of the Crimean Tatars. Above all, n the the Palace has the limestone mountains, pristine forest slopes, and orchards.Khan's Palace is a complex containing majestic mosques, menacing courtrooms, a hidden harem, a fountain of tears, and sorrowful tombs. The earliest dated construction in this ensemble bears the date of 1532, while the written records mention the Palace under 1539.The Palace stretches more than 50000 square meters and consists of 17 buildings and 9 courtyards. So,the overall architectural ambiance of the Palace is a careful amalgam of Middle Eastern and Crimean Tatar tradition. Moreover gardens and a life-giving, sustaining, and purifying supply of water is the focal point of the Palace’s design. The Big Khan Mosque is one of the oldest structures in the Palace, dating back to 1532, in short of the best heritage of cultural tourism. The Mosque is one of the largest in Crimea and bears the name of Sahib I Giray as its commissioner. The entry into the mosque is from a portal facing north. In addition, the mosque is made by Ottoman-designed. The roof, a narthex, and porticos are covering the main prayer hall. From the porticos, rise two minarets to the height of 28 meters.The minarets are octagonal and adorned with conical tops and finials. The lead and glass are decorating the minarets with imitation stones. The walls of the Mosque contain murals; depicting Quranic inscriptions and Islamic symbology. The calligraphic adeptness of these murals is phenomenal and bears a proud testimony to the skills of Persian artists. To sum up, the murals appear in green cartouches on the main façade of the Mosque and add to the charm of wood and plasterwork.

programme.desc: Los tesoros de una isla. La Isla de la Belleza, territorio francés de paisajes poderosos y naturaleza salvaje, ha sido conquistada a menudo, pero nunca sometida. Cultiva su carácter y su diferencia.

programme.title: Encuentros Que Generan Bienestar
programme.desc: Encuentros y conversaciones con personas, proyectos y experiencias que promueven el bienestar y una vida mas consciente. A traves de historias vinculadas al deporte, la naturaleza, la salud y el desarrollo personal, cada episodio invita a descubrir nuevas formas de vivir con equilibrio.

programme.title: Fraulein
programme.desc: Ruža left her home country Serbia over 30 years ago and now lives in Zurich. Her daily life is painstakingly organized but one day, Ana arrives on the scene. Ana, a young woman from Sarajevo, is beautiful, hungry for life yet somehow lost, and she shakes up Ruza's world. Nonetheless, a tender friendship develops between these two headstrong women.

programme.title: Bella Solitaria
programme.desc: Go Dok Mi es una editora de libros, bastante tímida, se niega a abandonar su apartamento o interactuar con la gente de su alrededor lo mayor posible. Cada día, ella recibe de forma anónima una caja de leche con un Post-it pegado, el que sigue una historia uno tras otro. Todos los días, usando un par de binoculares de color amarillo ella mira a su vecino de enfrente, Han Tae Joon. La última vez que estuvo fuera, fue en un parque en un día de otoño, se había enamorado de Tae Joon, a primera vista, lo continuo mirando y se dio cuenta que adoptó un perro. Cuando miró por la ventana y vio que el vivía en el apartamento de al frente, ella lo asocio al destino.

programme.title: Tel Afek (Fort Antipatris), Israel
programme.desc: Antipatris est un site archeologique riche situe sur la cote mediterraneenne israelienne. La ville fortifiee de Tel Afek, a mi-chemin entre Jerusalem et Cesaree, se trouve aujourd’hui dans un parc calme et silencieux. Le site est proche des sources perennes de la riviere Yarkon et fait desormais partie du parc national de Yarkon en Israel. Plus de 6 000 ans de villes successives se sont construites sur la colline surplombant les sources de la riviere Yarkon.

Il s’agit d’une eglise gothique construite par les Hospitaliers en 1140. En 1889, le gouvernement français acquiert ce magnifique monastere et le site passe sous la supervision des peres benedictins français.

programme.title: Des Racines et des ailes - Passion Patrimoine

programme.desc: Des Pyrenees espagnoles ou elle prend sa source, au vaste estuaire de la Gironde ou elle se jette, la Garonne parcourt plus de 600 kilometres a travers le Comminges, l'Agenais ou l'Entre-deux-Mers. Le fleuve evolue au cours de ce long voyage. L'apport de ses affluents, comme la Neste, l'Ariege, le Tarn et le Lot, modifie son visage. A bord d'un helicoptere, Didier Taillefer part en Espagne pour faire des photos aeriennes de l'une des principales sources du fleuve : le Trou du Toro. Ce site exceptionnel est situe au pied du massif de la Maladeta, ou la Garonne disparaît sous terre avant de reapparaître au Val d'Artan. Au coeur des Pyrenees, le fleuve donne naissance a un jardin de Cocagne : le Comminges. Dans le village de Huos, Remy Martin a amenage un verger-potager bio sur un ancien meandre.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Stehen Hybrid-Autos vor dem Aus?
programme.desc: Der Hybrid, also die Kombination aus Verbrenner und Elektromotor, hat aufgrund seiner Eigenschaften einige Erfolge verzeichnet. Er führte die Kunden an die Elektromobilität heran, bot aber gleichzeitig die Sicherheit, auf Langstrecken ohne Bedenken und ohne ständige Pausen voranzukommen. Reine Elektroautos müssen sich heute dank höheren Reichweiten auch nicht mehr verstecken. Gerät der Hybrid zunehmend in Vergessenheit? Alexander Bloch klärt auf!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Tesla Model 3 Highland: Weltklasse, aber patzt in manchen Sachen
programme.desc: Das Tesla Model 3 galt zeitweise als meistverkauftes Elektroauto in Deutschland und auf dem Kontinent. Was macht Tesla so besonders und was kann das neue Update? Alex Bloch bittet das frisch geliftete Tesla Model 3 Highland zum ersten Check.

programme.title: Vorfahrt
programme.desc: Brandaktuelle Tests, Service Informationen, die schnellsten Sportwagen der Welt – alles Wissenswerte und Spannende rund ums Auto!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Lancia Delta HF
programme.desc: Als Autotester kommt Alex immer wieder in den Genuss, besondere Autos zu fahren. Heute darf er seinen absoluten Traumwagen fahren. Für den Lancia Delta HF Integrale würde er so manchen Supersportwagen links liegen lassen. Wie sich Alex während der Fahrt bis über beide Ohren verliebt, seht ihr hier im Video.

programme.title: Bloch spielt - Miniatur Wunderland
programme.desc: Das Miniatur Wunderland in Hamburg ist das Paradies für alle Modellbau-Fans. Hier fahren Züge, Schiffe und Autos durch liebevoll und kreativ gestaltete Mini-Landschaften. Alexander Bloch bekommt heute eine exklusive Tour vom Modellbau-Papst: Gerrit Braun. Er zeigt Alex die Highlights des Miniatur Wunderlands und gewährt ihm einen Blick hinter die Kulissen. Eine Fahrt auf dem Formel1-Kurs von Monaco rundet die Tour ab.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Wechsel Sommerreifen
programme.desc: Der Frühling steht vor der Tür: Mit den steigenden Temperaturen rückt ein Punkt bei vielen Autofahrern wieder ganz nach oben: Der Wechsel auf Sommerreifen. Alex Bloch zeigt, dass man dabei viel falsch machen kann und gibt Tipps wie es richtig läuft.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Verbrauchs-Irrtümer!
programme.desc: Je schneller man beschleunigt, desto mehr verbraucht das Auto. Stimmt das eigentlich? Wenn es um den Energie-Bedarf von Autos geht, hat da so jeder seine eigenen Theorien und Tricks. Dabei entstehen auch Irrtümer und die klärt Alexander Bloch im Video auf.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Laden Elektro-Autos
programme.desc: Stecker rein und aufladen? So einfach wie das Volltanken beim Verbrenner ist die Energieversorgung eines Elektro-Autos (noch) nicht. Durch die teils riesigen Unterschiede bei der Ladetechnik entstehen viele Irrtümer. Mit den 8 größten räumt Alexander Bloch im Video auf.

programme.title: Einzeltest
programme.desc: Brandaktuelle Tests, Service Informationen, die schnellsten Sportwagen der Welt – alles Wissenswerte und Spannende rund ums Auto.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Mercedes-Benz EQS450
programme.desc: Heute im E-Auto Supertest mit Alexander Bloch - der Mercedes-Benz EQS 450+. Der Schwabe rühmt sich das beste E-Auto der Welt zu sein. Aber stimmt das wirklich? Reicht eine theoretische Reichweite von bis zu 780 Kilometern aus, um ein gutes E-Auto zu sein? Alexander Bloch jagt den Elektro-Stern durch den Supertest und findet heraus wie gut der EQS wirklich ist.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Audi Q4 50 e-tron
programme.desc: Auf dem MEB des Volkswagen-Konzerns entstehen zahlreiche E-Autos. Auch Audi nutzt die Plattform für den Q4 50 e-tron. Ist er damit nur ein teurer VW mit vier Ringen oder doch ein waschechter Audi? Alexander Bloch nimmt das Elektro-SUV genau unter die Lupe: Wie ist die Qualität? Wie gut ist die Bedienung? Welcher Verbrauch und welche Reichweite sind drin? Lädt der Audi Q4 50 e-tron wirklich schnell? Die Antworten gibt es im E-Auto-Supertest. Das wird gut!

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Der Fiat 500 Elektro
programme.desc: Fiat hat kräftig an seinem Kult-Mini - dem 500 - gefeilt. Die neue Generation kommt als vollelektrischer Kleinstwagen. Altbekanntes Design mit komplett neuer E-Technik. Kann der Italiener mit der Konkurrenz mithalten? Heute stellt sich der Fiat 500 Elektro dem E-Auto Supertest von Alexander Bloch. Wie gut lädt er? Wie groß ist die Reichweite? Wie sind Qualität und E-Auto-Ausstattung? Und vor allem: Wo findet er sich im Gesamt-Ranking wieder?

programme.title: Fast Lap
programme.desc: Brandaktuelle Tests, Service Informationen, die schnellsten Sportwagen der Welt – alles Wissenswerte und Spannende rund ums Auto.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Mercedes E-Actros 600: Die 5 GIGA-Fakten zum neuen Elektro-Truck
programme.desc: Mercedes-Benz Trucks präsentiert den E-Actros 600, einen batterieelektrischen 40-Tonner, der ohne Zwischenladung mehr als 500 Kilometer weit fahren soll. Alexander Bloch durfte sich den Elektro-LKW bereits exklusiv anschauen und erklärt die 5 Giga-Fakten zum neuen Mercedes E-Actros 600.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Sparen mit dem Elektroauto: Das bringt was - und das bringt nichts!
programme.desc: Auch zum Elektroauto gibt es eine Vielzahl an Spartipps. Doch bringen die wirklich was? Alexander Bloch erklärt welche Tipps sinnvoll sind - und welche ihr euch sparen könnt.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Langstreckenstar Hyundai Ioniq 6: Fast wie ein Verbrenner!
programme.desc: Oft fließt die Reichenweitenangst in die Kaufentscheidung von Elektro-Autos ein. Bei Verbrennern stellt sich diese Frage gar nicht: die Reichweiten sind hoch und nach einem fünfminütigen Tankstopp geht es für gewöhnlich weiter. Eignen sich Elektro-Autos auch als Reisebegleiter? Wie viel Reichweite ist wirklich nötig? Und wie viel Zeit muss ich für das Laden einplanen? All das beantwortet Alexander Bloch anhand des Hyundai Ioniq 6.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Ist Drehmoment wichtiger als Leistung? Die 5 größten Irrtümer zu PS & Co.
programme.desc: PS, Kilowatt und Newtonmeter benutzt man häufig, wenn man über Autos spricht. Dabei gibt es hier einige Stolperfallen. Sind PS in allen Ländern gleich? Newtonmeter gibt es nur beim Drehmoment? Alexander Bloch erklärt die 5 größten Irrtümer zu PS, Kilowatt und Co.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Kein Motoröl im E-Auto? 4 Irrtümer zu Öl im Elektroauto
programme.desc: Ein E-Auto braucht kein Öl und schon gar kein Motoröl. Ist das wirklich so? Chief Explanation Officer Alexander Bloch ist ins Forschungs- und Entwicklungszentrum von Petronas Lubricants gefahren, um mit den größten Öl-Irrtümern rund um die Elektromobilität und die Zukunft von Schmier- und Motorölen aufzuräumen.

programme.desc: Porsche hat den Taycan umfangreich überarbeitet und in vielen Disziplinen verbessert. Die Batterie wird größer und kann schneller Laden. Alex Bloch fährt den Basis Taycan mit großer Batterie im E-Auto-Supertest und kommt aus dem Grinsen nicht mehr raus. Wie die Chancen stehen, dass der Taycan auf die Pole Position der Elektroautos fährt, seht ihr im Video.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der MG4 Electric im E-Auto Supertest
programme.desc: Der MG4 schwimmt auf der Erfolgswelle! Der Überflieger befindet sich unter den Top 5 der meistverkauften Elektroautos in Deutschland. Was der chinesischen Kompaktstromer im Vergleich zum Opel Astra Electric und dem VW ID.3 drauf hat, klärt Alexander Bloch.

programme.title: E-Auto Supertest - Top oder Flop? Der Opel Astra Electric im EAS
programme.desc: Kein anderes Auto hat Alexander Bloch bisher in ein solches Wechselbad der Gefühle geschmissen. Von „sensationell!“ bis „macht ihr Witze?“ ist alles dabei. Was die Stärken und Schwächen des Opel Astra Electric sind und ob er sich gegen den VW ID.3 behaupten kann, erfahrt ihr hier!

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Comeback des Wankelmotors - So fährt sich der Mazda MX-30 R-EV
programme.desc: Im Mazda MX-30 R-EV sorgt ein Wankelmotor für den Strom der E-Maschine - ein sogenannter Range Extender. Wie sich das ungewöhnliche Konzept fährt und was es für Vorteile hat, findet Alexander Bloch heraus.

programme.title: Bloch spielt - Traxxas X Maxx
programme.desc: Der Traxxas Xmaxx ist ein wahres Monster unter den RC-Cars. Mit satten 6 PS und einer Spitzengeschwindigkeit von 80 km/h rollt der Traxxas über die Motocross-Strecke des MSC Kleinhau.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - Porsche 911 T
programme.desc: Porsche 911 T mit Ölklappe sind nicht dafür bekannt besonders günstig zu sein. Doch dieses Modell kostet 1.000.000 €. Warum das so ist erklärt Alexander Bloch in dieser Folge Bloch erklärt.

programme.title: Bloch erklärt - 5 x Auto-Technik, die unlogisch erscheint
programme.desc: Höheres Gewicht bringt einen kürzeren Bremsweg, Elektromotoren beschleunigen und bremsen gleichzeitig und größere Verbrennungsmotoren, die effizienter sind als kleine: In der Auto-Technik gibt es einige Dinge, die auf den ersten Blick unlogisch wirken. Ob sie das wirklich sind, klärt Alexander Bloch.

programme.title: Planet Of The Sharks
programme.desc: In un futuro non troppo lontano, lo scioglimento dei ghiacciai ha coperto d'acqua il 98% del pianeta. In questo scenario, gli squali hanno preso il sopravvento guidati da un esemplare geneticamente mutato. I pochi umani sopravvissuti vivono nel terrore ma ben presto un piccolo gruppo di disperati tenterà tutto il possibile per rendere le acque nuovamente sicure.

programme.title: 20.0 Megaquake
programme.desc: Mentre un mega-terremoto minaccia San Francisco, una serie di scosse di preavviso crea scompiglio in tutta la città. Una squadra d'élite di esperti di servizi di emergenza e di catastrofi converge sull'epicentro previsto, lavorando instancabilmente per salvare quante più vite possibili prima che la città venga schiacciata nell'oblio.

programme.title: San Andreas Quake
programme.desc: Dopo aver avuto la carriera screditata a causa di un incidente, una sismologa mette in guardia la popolazione circa un terremoto di proporzioni immani che colpirà Los Angeles, ma nessuno le crede.

programme.title: Blackout - Invasion Earth
programme.desc: In un futuro prossimo, la Russia viene colpita da un blackout. Ogni comunicazione è interrotta, le città sono al buio. Nella nuova e inquietante dimensione d'isolamento milioni di persone impazziscono e muoiono per cause sconosciute. Chi si nasconde dietro il disfacimento della nazione e il collasso del mondo intero? A una squadra di eroi, il compito di salvare quel che rimane dell'umanità.

programme.title: Ice 2020 - Parte 1
programme.desc: E ‘il 2020. I risultati di uno scienziato ambientale, il Professor Thom Archer suggeriscono che Halo, l’impresa di perforazione della società energetica sul ghiacciaio della Groenlandia ne stanno causando lo scioglimento. Gli avvertimenti di Archer vengono ignorati, così si dirige verso l’Artico per trovare prove inconfutabili. Al suo arrivo, si rende conto che l’umanità è in pericolo immediato, e corre a casa per salvare la sua famiglia. Il ghiacciaio collassa, con conseguenze devastanti...

programme.title: End Of The World
programme.desc: Mentre una massa di tempeste solari provoca tsunami, vulcani e inondazioni, una famiglia tenta di fuggire dalla città verso la relativa salvezza in un gruppo di grotte ad alta quota a diverse miglia di distanza dall'occhio del ciclone.

programme.title: Alien Convergence
programme.desc: Una squadra, composta da persone con disabilità fisiche, sviluppa un rivoluzionario progetto per pilotare gli aerei da combattimento attraverso un collegamento neurale. Quando dalla NASA scoprono che qualcosa sta per entrare nell'atmosfera, tale progetto viene messo in atto per respingere un'invasione aliena.

programme.title: Kill Mode
programme.desc: Otto anni dopo lo scoppio di un'epidemia, il mondo è controllato da un'industria farmaceutica chiamata The Company. Ma il suo scopo è veramente quello di preservare l'umanità? David Oscar, un ex combattente per la libertà, scoprirà un inquietante segreto che potrebbe far crollare per sempre la compagnia che possiede il mondo.

programme.title: 500 Mph Storm - Mega Tornado
programme.desc: Quando viene perso il controllo di un esperimento energetico, una gran quantità di uragani si abbatte sul Nord America. Un insegnante di scienze del liceo cercherà di mettere in salvo la sua famiglia prima dell'arrivo degli uragani, creando un "hypercane", un uragano potente abbastanza da annullare gli altri, ma in grado anche di cancellare gli Stati Uniti dalla faccia della Terra.

programme.title: 2025: Armageddon
programme.desc: Una razza aliena attacca la Terra utilizzando creature giganti e catastrofi naturali ispirate ai film trasmessi dal canale The Asylum's Movie Channel, che ha raggiunto il loro pianeta. Un gruppo di eroi improbabili deve unire le forze per fermare la distruzione e salvare il mondo da una catastrofe imminente.

programme.desc: From tropical coffee aromas to high-tech computing hubs, how is China defining "high-quality development"? programme.title: Wudang Martial Arts and Taichi
programme.desc: Join host Yegor on a journey into the heart of China’s Wudang Mountains—the spiritual cradle of Taoism and the birthplace of Wudang martial arts. Through in-depth conversations with renowned masters such as Zhong Xueyong, Cai Chongguang, Jake Pinnick, and Liu Xiang, this episode explores the philosophy, techniques, and living spirit of Wudang Quan and Taichi. From the internal cultivation of qi to the harmony between body and mind, Wudang martial arts are more than just physical training—they are a way of life rooted in the Tao. Alongside martial techniques, the program also delves into traditional Chinese music, calligraphy, and medicine, revealing how these disciplines come together in the pursuit of balance, self-awareness, and longevity. This is not just a story of punches and postures, but of tradition, transformation, and the timeless search for harmony between humans and the universe.

programme.title: Young Shaolin master
programme.desc: Xu Haican is a kung fu practitioner at the Quanzhou Shaolin Temple in Fujian. The 12-year-old boy is now an expert with the sword, the nine-section chain whip, and the monkey stick after just two years of training. Xu said these weapons give him both confidence and discipline, as he must wield them safely in practice. The young Shaolin master said he hopes to learn more from his masters and carry forward the Chinese martial art.

programme.title: Mount Wutai, Embracing the Wonders of Nature
programme.desc: Mount Wutai, in the northeastern part of Shanxi Province, is one of the Four Great Buddhist Mountains of China. It is a magnet for tourists, who are drawn here not only by its profound Buddhist cultural heritage, but also by the spectacular natural scenery. Mount Wutai is noted for its unique topography, marked by five flattened peaks. Hence the name "Wutai," or “Five Terraces.” The five, each with its own characteristics and distinct shape, are Wanghai East Peak, Guayue West Peak, Jinxiu South Peak, Yedou North Peak, and Cuiyan Central Peak. Soaring into the clouds, together they resemble a magnificent work crafted by nature.

programme.title: Chengdu Lacquerware Art
programme.desc: Chengdu lacquerware is unique, thanks to its “three carvings and one engraving” technique. Along with its bold decorative style, this has made it a gem of Chinese lacquer art. Chengdu lacquerware also emphasizes the use of vibrant colors. Pieces are brought to beautiful life by bright red, vivid yellow, emerald green, and other striking hues.

programme.title: Forged in Legend: A Glimpse of Longquan Blades
programme.desc: Longquan swords, legendary blades from China, embody centuries of masterful craftsmanship. Forged with unique folding techniques and a distinctive star-patterned finish, these swords are renowned for their sharpness, resilience, and artistic value. Discover the rich history and cultural significance of these revered symbols of Chinese heritage.

programme.title: CULTURAL INHERITORS “Tribute tea” to more tea lovers

The eight episodes span across various regions of China, focusing on the inheritors and artists of intangible cultural heritage. They explore and innovate with artisanal dedication, showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship of fields such as the Ru Kiln porcelain, colored stone inlay, Pu'er tea, and Lingnan woodwork. programme.title: World Heritages in China: A Journey on Water from Wuxi to Yixing
programme.desc: Water has always been the heartbeat of human civilization, nurturing the cities it weaves through. From the first drops that carved out its waterways to the thriving metropolis we see today, Wuxi’s story is inseparable from the grand canal. This is the story of a city born of water. In this episode, we uncover how the waters have shaped Wuxi’s identity.

programme.title: Wudang Martial Arts and Taichi
programme.desc: Join host Yegor on a journey into the heart of China’s Wudang Mountains—the spiritual cradle of Taoism and the birthplace of Wudang martial arts. Through in-depth conversations with renowned masters such as Zhong Xueyong, Cai Chongguang, Jake Pinnick, and Liu Xiang, this episode explores the philosophy, techniques, and living spirit of Wudang Quan and Taichi. From the internal cultivation of qi to the harmony between body and mind, Wudang martial arts are more than just physical training—they are a way of life rooted in the Tao. Alongside martial techniques, the program also delves into traditional Chinese music, calligraphy, and medicine, revealing how these disciplines come together in the pursuit of balance, self-awareness, and longevity. This is not just a story of punches and postures, but of tradition, transformation, and the timeless search for harmony between humans and the universe.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of black-necked cranes
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: The Great Wall Homestay
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, Tianran He's heading to the mountains on Beijing’s northern outskirts, to meet some people his age who have swapped city life for the chance to run guesthouses beside the Great Wall of China.

programme.title: A Village Homestay in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, our presenter Tianran He’s heading out of Beijing proper, to the city’s Miyun District. There he’ll meet some people running guesthouses who gave up their day jobs, in order to achieve the dream of a place of their own in the country.

programme.title: Young Shaolin master
programme.desc: Xu Haican is a kung fu practitioner at the Quanzhou Shaolin Temple in Fujian. The 12-year-old boy is now an expert with the sword, the nine-section chain whip, and the monkey stick after just two years of training. Xu said these weapons give him both confidence and discipline, as he must wield them safely in practice. The young Shaolin master said he hopes to learn more from his masters and carry forward the Chinese martial art.

programme.title: Mount Wutai, Embracing the Wonders of Nature
programme.desc: Mount Wutai, in the northeastern part of Shanxi Province, is one of the Four Great Buddhist Mountains of China. It is a magnet for tourists, who are drawn here not only by its profound Buddhist cultural heritage, but also by the spectacular natural scenery. Mount Wutai is noted for its unique topography, marked by five flattened peaks. Hence the name "Wutai," or “Five Terraces.” The five, each with its own characteristics and distinct shape, are Wanghai East Peak, Guayue West Peak, Jinxiu South Peak, Yedou North Peak, and Cuiyan Central Peak. Soaring into the clouds, together they resemble a magnificent work crafted by nature.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: Harmony Keepers: Guardians of milu deer
programme.desc: This documentary series pays tribute to the guardians of China’s rare wildlife and their habitats. Through the lens of ecological protection and preservation, the series features four iconic protected species in China: the Tibetan antelope, milu deer, black-necked cranes, and golden snub-nosed monkeys.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, traveling to the cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan to meet another group of extraordinary women. By capturing snippets of the lives and work of an electric locomotive designer, a flight instructor, a painter, and a poverty alleviation volunteer, we showcase the unique cultural and humanistic charm of this region.

programme.title: Ancient tradition in an old town takes on new life
programme.desc: The Chinese lion dance is an art form that combines acrobatics, dance, folk music and embroidery. The southern style lion dance was a staple in the ancient town of Qiantong before the costume faded in the early 20th century. However, now the tradition has been revived by some incredible talented young people from this town.

programme.title: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River
programme.desc: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River is a documentary focusing on the World Heritage sites and cultural–ecological conservation in the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Through the lens of Ningxia’s heritage stories, the film highlights China’s commitment to World Heritage preservation, ecological restoration, and cultural continuity — presenting to global audiences a land where history and modernity intertwine, and where desert and oasis coexist. By following the guardians of the Western Xia Imperial Tombs, desert restorers in the Tengger Desert, Great Wall rangers at Sanguankou, traditional sheepskin raft craftsmen, and managers of the Yellow River irrigation system in Qingtongxia, the program reveals Ningxia’s distinctive contributions to cultural heritage, natural ecology, and intangible traditions — and the enduring human spirit behind them.

programme.title: A Lifelong Journey of Xuan Paper
programme.desc: The host travels to Jingxian, Anhui—known as the hometown of Xuan paper—to experience the intricate process of making this traditional paper. Along the way, they uncover the secrets behind its thousand-year legacy and witness the craftsmanship of Xuan paper inheritors at every stage. Through vivid, personal stories, the episode reveals the hidden struggles and quiet perseverance that have kept this intangible cultural heritage alive across generations.

programme.title: Awakening Lion
programme.desc: Xingshi, or literally “awakened lion,” is a name for the southern style of the lion dance. Historically, it evolved from a court dance in the Tang Dynasty almost 1,200 years ago. With the southward migration of the population from the central plains, lion dance culture was introduced to the south. In the Ming Dynasty around 400 years ago, xingshi appeared in Guangdong and was then widely spread throughout southern China and even overseas. Lion dance has become a very important part of Chinese culture.

programme.title: CULTURAL INHERITORS Inheritance matters more than fame
programme.desc: The Vibe production team's meticulously crafted documentary series "Cultural Inheritors". The eight episodes span across various regions of China, focusing on the inheritors and artists of intangible cultural heritage. They explore and innovate with artisanal dedication, showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship of fields such as the Ru Kiln porcelain, colored stone inlay, Pu'er tea, and Lingnan woodwork. Let’s embark on a cultural journey together, savoring the beauty of tradition and embracing the spirit of intangible cultural heritage!

programme.title: Miao Embroidery: History in Stitches
programme.desc: According to legend, during a migration by the Miao ethnic group, a female chieftain wanted to keep a record of all the mountains and lakes she passed along the way. The means she chose of doing so was by stitching the images on her dress. By the time they reached a suitable place to settle, her clothing was covered with embroidered designs. This, it’s said, was the origin of Miao embroidery. As the story tells us, the designs in Miao embroidery are closely related to the natural world and daily life. The Miao people have a special fondness for nature. So, as well as depicting their daily farming and work activities, they copy birds, flowers, mountains, and grass onto their clothing. Over the years, the embroidery of the Miao people has become a written record of their life. The stitches are like characters which, when many of them are combined, become a record of their history, their collected wisdom, and the knowledge passed down from their ancestors.

programme.title: Quyang Stone Carving
programme.desc: Quyang is known as a hometown of Chinese carving. Quyang's stone carving works are popular around different parts of China, thus also exported to over 100 countries and regions worldwide. The style of Quyang stone carving both carries the mysterious and rough spirit of the Wei Dynasty and the natural and graceful forms of the Tang and Song dynasties. It reflects the life experiences and live philosophies of local artisans. Each statue's showcases unique oriental aesthetics.

programme.title: Cobardes
programme.desc: Gaby, un pelirrojo de 14 ańos en Barcelona, sufre constantes robos y palizas a manos de Guille y su despiadada pandilla, quienes lo apodan "Zanahoria". Incapaz de compartir su sufrimiento con sus padres, siempre ocupados con sus trabajos, Gaby se encierra en sí mismo mientras el bullying se intensifica. La madre de Guille encuentra un video violento en el móvil de su hijo y, aunque lo borra, Guille niega todo y se presenta como víctima ante el psicólogo escolar. La historia da un giro inesperado cuando el dueńo de la pizzería favorita de Gaby, un mafioso secreto, podría tener una pista que cambiará radicalmente las cosas. La situación se complica aún más cuando los padres de los involucrados, absortos en sus propios problemas, no logran percibir la magnitud del sufrimiento de Gaby, dejándolo cada vez más aislado y vulnerable.

programme.title: Viento Aparte
programme.desc: La madre de Omar (15) y Karina (12) sufre un derrame cerebral durante las vacaciones familiares. Abandonados a su suerte, los hermanos iniciarán un largo viaje a través de México hacia la casa de su abuela.

programme.title: La suerte dormida
programme.desc: Una mujer defiende un caso judicial de indemnizacion por muerte y su vida cambia.

programme.desc: Ernesto choca su auto con el de Gloria para salvarle la vida, sin sospechar las consecuencias que ello traerá a su vida.

programme.desc: Maria, una enfermera cuya hija fue asesinada por tres paramilitares, viaja desde Colombia a España con su hijo menor para vengarse.

programme.desc: La vida de Antonio tiembla con el regreso de Carolina, su mejor amiga a la que no ha visto en 6 años. Esta vez, sus planes cambian - el amor comienza a jugar con su corazón.
